title: In Ordinary Times
subtitle: Sharing secrets is how conspiracies form.

trails.title: Open the Door of Fate
trails.description: Some prophecies take ages to come true. Others, only a moment.

content.text:
She must have foreseen this moment before.
The clean lines of the dark marble floor before her match the image in her mind. The visitors' shapes are just as they appeared in the orbuculum. The woman with black-rimmed glasses and dark eyes is kinder but firmer than expected. Blue top hat, distant look—a familiar childhood friend.
And then ... a duckling. She flaps her wings as she rushes up the steps, the sound of leather shoes stomping loudly. She doesn't apologize for bumping into anyone ... First floor, second. The hallways of the Foundation seem endless today ... No need to ask for directions, she runs, panting, sure of where she's going ...

"Please leave the door, Vertin. I'm expecting more company," she says quietly.
A glance passes between the one in the blue hat and the one with glasses, who gives a slight nod.

Footsteps approach quickly, accompanied by the sound of labored breathing. There's no knock. The door, already slightly ajar, is pushed wide open.
"Ha! Mama! *deep breath* I knew I'd find you here!"

trails.title: The Opposite of Perjury
trails.description: She shows no change in expression, her pulse steady, her statement flawless.

content.text: Ah, a visitor. How unexpected. There is nothing here now—only the ashes of war. What is it you want from a place like this?
Run along now. Back to your schoolbooks ... or a swing in a playground, perhaps. This is no place for a girl like you.

branch.text: Naturally. I am no celebrity.
I'd prefer to keep it that way.
Fame is of no interest to me. Just an opportunity for greater harassment.
Then you and I are in agreement.
The stench of rust and burnt flesh is quite unbearable.
Even the maggots squirming over the soldiers' corpses have summoned all their strength just to crawl away.
But the entire world is in ruins now. I have nowhere else to go.
And it seems you're stuck here with me. You poor sap.
You trekked to the end of the world, fought a pointless war, and for what? A broken spinning wheel?
Even that, they took away from you—along with the girl clinging to life by a thread—before sending you off to the next battleground.
I hope that rusty old thing holds SOME kind of secret—to saving the world, or ending this war.
Maybe then, you can take on another career before you die. A watchmaker, perhaps.
The war will end one day.
I've nothing more to say. Would you kindly leave me alone for a while?
I have no tea or snacks to offer. I can't even recall what they taste like.
Go on. Savor the war. There'll be another after this. No need to worry about things going exactly as you'd like.

Go on. Savor the war. There'll be another after this. No need to worry about things going exactly as you'd like.
I have reasons to continue the fight.

items.text: Interrogation Room, Vigiles Bureau

items.speaker: Vigil Officer
items.text: So, let me get this straight: The fifth "Storm" was brought forth by Manus Vindictae, and you witnessed the process firsthand.

items.speaker: Vigil Officer
items.text: Based on your testimony, Ms. Beryl Bouanich wasn't an accomplice of the Manus, and she even saved your life.

items.speaker: Brume
items.text: Yes.
The mist clears from the black mirror, revealing the witness beneath—it was never a lie.

items.speaker: Vigil Officer
items.text: And after that? What happened?

items.speaker: Brume
items.text: I followed Madame Bouanich's advice and made it to a shelter that could resist the "Storm."

items.speaker: Brume
items.text: The rain got heavier and heavier along the way, but thankfully, we made it there just in time.

items.speaker: Brume
items.text: It's such a shame my little cab didn't have room for anyone else.

items.speaker: Brume
items.text: I know that there's still a Paris out there, but it's no longer my Paris.

items.speaker: Brume
items.text: Everything I loved there was washed away in the rain. Heh, just as the prophecy said.
The storyteller caps her story with a bitter laugh, leaving the room quiet.

items.speaker: Brume
items.text: And the rest ... you already know.

items.speaker: Brume
items.text: Thanks to Madame Bouanich, I wasn't left on the streets alone.

items.speaker: Brume
items.text: The neighborhoods I knew, the people I once recognized—they've all changed. But at least I have my car.

items.speaker: Brume
items.text: In any case, I still prefer driving the streets to staying in some cozy room.

items.speaker: Brume
items.text: Madame Bouanich's work keeps her on the move, so I've been helping her since then.

items.speaker: Brume
items.text: We even went to Delhi to sell her topazes. Oh, and I met her daughter there—Matilda.

items.speaker: Brume
items.text: She's nothing like her mother. Everything she feels is written plainly on her face. To be honest, I get along better with her.

items.speaker: Brume
items.text: Madame Bouanich ... She's changed, too.
She pauses.

items.speaker: Brume
items.text: She feels more real now. More alive.
Their conversation continues for some time before ending, until, after the sound of departing footsteps, silence returns.

items.speaker: Black Ibis's Cadet
items.text: It seems Ms. Bouanich is in the clear, based on the witness's testimony.

items.speaker: Black Ibis's Cadet
items.text: She claims Beryl Bouanich saved her and has remained at her side for years. If there were anything suspicious going on, she would've noticed.

items.speaker: Black Ibis
items.text: Hmm. I wouldn't be so sure.
A voice comes from the shadowed corner. Throughout the inquiry, his superior has kept silent.

items.speaker: Black Ibis's Cadet
items.text: You don't trust the lie detector results? Isn't this the most advanced, top-of-the-line model?

items.speaker: Black Ibis
items.text: Advanced or not, machines can fail. I prefer to trust my instincts.
Black Ibis steps out from the dark, rapping her knuckles on that costly "top-of-the-line model" on the table.

items.speaker: Black Ibis
items.text: And mine are telling me—she's hiding something.

items.speaker: Black Ibis's Cadet
items.text: About the fifth "Storm"?

items.speaker: Black Ibis
items.text: That, and the fact that Madame Bouanich returned so abruptly.

items.speaker: Black Ibis
items.text: After the ninth "Storm," she vanished without a trace. Who would've thought—

items.speaker: Black Ibis
items.text: She would stroll back in out of nowhere, acting as if nothing happened, with some "big revelation" in hand.
The corridor is empty but for one still figure.

items.speaker: Voice in Head
items.text: Unbelievable. One sloppy mistake after another.

items.speaker: Voice in Head
items.text: You'd have been less conspicuous if you'd just written "liar" all over your face. You should count yourself lucky I covered for you.
Brume hadn't planned to answer, but the voice is incessant.

items.speaker: Brume
items.text: Are you expecting a thank you from me, Félicienne?

items.speaker: Brume
items.text: Don't think I don't know. You just don't want your own secrets exposed.

items.speaker: Brume
items.text: And didn't I tell you to stop talking to me like this while we're on Foundation grounds? Who knows who might be eavesdropping on us?

items.speaker: Félicienne
items.text: And I told you that I can hear you perfectly well without you mouthing the words. Is that really so hard to understand?

items.speaker: Brume
items.text: And if I slip up subconsciously?

items.speaker: Brume
items.text: I suppose you might have forgotten what it feels like to have a mouth.
A cold snort crawls from her left hand up through her arm and rattles around her skull.

items.speaker: Félicienne
items.text: Always so rude to me, while you offer nothing but praise and fawning to that woman.

items.speaker: Félicienne
items.text: You ought to have listened to me—gone to meet the Guiding One and pledged your loyalty. But you didn't because you are, and always have been, a stubborn fool.

items.speaker: Félicienne
items.text: Fine. Side with the Foundation if you want. Call it ignorance, call it shortsightedness—should I expect anything less from such rabble?

items.speaker: Félicienne
items.text: But staking our lives on that woman? That is something far more than simply foolish! Do you really trust her so much?
The complaining voice in her head receives a curt reply.

items.speaker: Brume
items.text: I do. I believe in Madame Bouanich.

items.speaker: Brume
items.text: She'll prove I made the right choice.
A knock on the door. A pause. The chief of staff's voice from within.

items.speaker: Z
items.text: Who is it?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: It's me, Vertin. I've come to check on the status of my field mission application.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Is now not a good time?
Usually the door opens right away, but this time she waits a little longer.

items.speaker: Z
items.text: Please. Come in, Vertin.
She pushes it open. A stranger sits on the guest sofa.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: We finally meet, Ms. Vertin. Matilda has told me much about you.
The name of an old classmate resurfaces. The woman's refined features blur with another livelier face.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Then you must be Madame Beryl Bouanich?

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: I see we can skip the formalities.
Her smile is warm and gentle, but her eyes don't match.

items.speaker: Beryl
items.text: You have seen the golden thread, have you not?
